record.original_question: In rules for computing dag-solved forms of unification problems in equational theories, can the Merge rule condition requiring s to be a non-variable no larger than t be replaced by the condition that Check* does not apply; equivalently, is Check* complete for finding cycles under this modified Merge rule?

evidence.quote: Can the application condition on the Merge rule in the computation of dag-solved forms of unification problems be improved?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a set of inference rules that transform a system of equations in an equational theory toward a "dag-solved form": a conjunction of equations x_1 = t_1, ..., x_n = t_n where the x_i are pairwise distinct variables and there is no cycle in the dependency relation x_i ▷ x_j defined by "x_j occurs in t_i" (so that the system, viewed as a substitution after acyclic ordering, is idempotent).

Among the transformation rules is a Merge rule of the form
    {x = s, x = t} ∪ P  ⟹  {x = t, s = t} ∪ P,
which combines two equations sharing the left-hand variable x. As usually stated, the Merge rule carries the application condition that s is a non-variable term whose size is no larger than the size of t (this restriction is imposed to ensure termination and to interact properly with an occurs-check style rule).

A separate rule, called Check*, is used to detect cycles in the variable-dependency graph of the current system and to signal failure when such a cycle is present.

Question. Can the application condition on the Merge rule "s is a non-variable term and |s| ≤ |t|" be replaced by the strictly more permissive condition "Check* does not apply to the current system" while preserving soundness, completeness and termination of the overall rule set for computing dag-solved forms? Equivalently, is Check* complete for detecting all cycles that would otherwise be prevented by the size/non-variable restriction on Merge?
